terms.gloss: have enough to do, have one’s hands full
terms.grammar: satis (sat) with agō, often written as one word
evidence: Cato in Charis.: jam apud vallum nostrī satis agēbant (Lewis & Short), s.v. satis
Plaut. Bacch. 4.3.23: nunc agitās sat tūte tuārum rērum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short s.v. satis: “to have enough to do, have one’s hands full; to be in trouble”. The thing that keeps one busy is in the genitive in comedy: sat agere suārum rērum.

sources: Lewis & Short: satis · Lewis & Short: satago
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 99, 325.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
